paper_title: Riding the dark matter wave: Novel limits on general dark photons from LISA Pathfinder
coupling_convention: epsilon_{B-L}, relative coupling strength as plotted on Fig. 3 y-axis (g_{B-L} = epsilon_{B-L} * e); values emitted exactly as plotted, NOT converted to g_BL
notes: Paper derives NEW limits on gauged B-L (and B) dark photon dark matter using LISA Pathfinder auxiliary SC-TM relative-acceleration channels (Apr 2016 noise data, ~6.5 days). World-leading in 4e-19 eV < m < 3e-17 eV. No numerical table is given; data points above are reconstructed from eq. (8) with SNR=1, Delta(q/M)_{B-L}=0.018 GeV^-1, rho_DM=0.4 GeV/cm^3, and ASD values read approximately from fig. 2 (peak ~1e-13 m/s^2/sqrt(Hz) at ~1e-3 Hz), so they are approximate (factor ~2-3 uncertainty). Peak sensitivity g_BL ~ few x 1e-27 at m ~ 4-5e-18 eV, consistent with the stated >2 orders of magnitude improvement over MICROSCOPE. Paper also gives B-coupling limits (~3 orders weaker) and LISA projections (is_projection false because the primary result is a data-derived limit). Limit set by demanding SNR <= 1, not a formal 90/95% CL. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('envelope of the solid red/green/orange 'LPF Apr 16 data' curves') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.7, 43)) | Vision: Traced the lower envelope of the solid red/green/orange 'LPF Apr 16 data' curves in Fig. 3 (main new result of the paper) on the epsilon_{B-L} vs DP mass plane. Curves span the analysis frequency cuts 1e-4 Hz to 1 Hz (m = 4.1e-19 to 4.1e-15 eV via m = 4.136e-15 f). Peak sensitivity epsilon ~ 3e-27 at ~5e-18 eV is confirmed by the paper text. Local maximum (star-tracker noise bump) at ~1.2e-18 eV. Note the y-axis of Fig. 3 is the relative coupling epsilon_{B-L}, not g_{B-L}; Fig. 5 shows the same limits converted to g_{B-L} = epsilon*e, but per the plotted-values contract I emit the Fig. 3 epsilon values since the axis calibration provided matches Fig. 3.
